source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. Persistent UCE on Primary Channel specific BIOS setup : • Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration > — Mirror Mode = Full Mirror Mode • Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > — Enforce Population POR = Disable • Disabling this knob is not required but was disabled because a non-POR memory population was used. It is highly recommended to have a POR memory population. 2. Complete steps 1-6 in the CE recipe to check on the state of the system, find an address to inject to, and to unlock the injectors. 3. Choose the target device for error injection and modify masks for a multi-device uncorrectable ECC error injection. >>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=1, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=2, dev1msk=0x3) 4. Inject a persistent uncorrectable ECC error and consume the error. >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(addr=0x000100000000, errType="uce", oneInjection=False, verbose=True) 5. Check the target B2CMI MC bank to verify that the injection was successful. For easier decoding, read the B2CMI shadow registers. For MCi_STATUS check that all the bit-fields are the same as shown next. MCi_ADDR should align with the injection address in the previous step. For MCi_MISC, the bit-fields of interest which should be logged as shown next are: mirrorfailover (mirror scrub failed and failover must occur), mccmdmirrregion (transaction was to a mirrored region), and bankindex (value should align with the memory controller of the injection target). >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_status_shadow >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_addr_shadow >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_misc_shadow >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_status_shadow.show() >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_misc_shadow.show() 6. Since the system is halted and mirror failover has not been configured by BIOS, ddr4chnlfailed is 0. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mirrorfailover.show() 7. Resume the system to allow all error handling flows to complete. >>> go() 8. After go(), MIRRORFAILOVER.ddr4chnlfailed on the primary channel should be "1" to indicate that the channel failed over. Also check that MIRRORFAILOVER on the secondary channel shows the primary channel has failed over to the secondary channel; buddychnlfailed should be "1". >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mirrorfailover.show() >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi1.mirrorfailover.show()

test_case.purpose: Demonstrate that a persistent primary-channel UCE in Full-Mirror mode causes failed mirror scrub and a controlled primary-to-secondary channel failover with the specified B2CMI state.
required_package: CScripts version/hash/license and exact CE-recipe dependency
Approved persistent-UCE masks and MCi_STATUS/MISC/failover values
Dedicated window, serial/OOB and degraded-channel recovery/restoration plan
